senses.title: Written works valued as art
senses.definition: novels, poems, plays and other writing valued for form and imagination rather than for information alone
senses.definitionCN: 小说、诗歌、戏剧等因其形式与想象力而受重视、而非只用来传递信息的写作
senses.example: She studied English literature at university.
senses.exampleCN: 她在大学学习英国文学。
senses.why: Litteratura first meant the act of writing and the learning that letters bring; the works carrying that learning took the name, and artistic writing moved to the centre.
senses.whyCN: litteratura 最初指书写这件事以及文字带来的学问；承载这种学问的作品接过了这个名字，艺术性的写作后来占据了中心。

senses.title: The body of writing on a subject
senses.definition: the books, articles and reports published about a particular subject, considered as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 关于某一主题已出版的书籍、文章与报告的整体
senses.example: The literature on climate change is now enormous.
senses.exampleCN: 关于气候变化的文献现在多得惊人。
senses.why: A subject keeps its knowledge in texts; once those texts pile up, scholars call the whole shelf the literature of the field, even when the writing is technical.
senses.whyCN: 一个学科把知识存放在文本里；文本一旦堆积起来，学者就把整排书架称作该领域的文献，即便那些文字是技术性的。

senses.title: The academic study of literary works
senses.definition: the subject taught and researched at universities that deals with novels, poems and plays
senses.definitionCN: 大学里讲授与研究小说、诗歌、戏剧的学科
senses.example: He teaches literature at a small college.
senses.exampleCN: 他在一所小学规模的学院教文学。
senses.why: A body of texts large enough to be taught turns into a subject; the noun for the works becomes the noun for the department that studies them.
senses.whyCN: 一批文本大到可以被讲授时，就变成了一个学科；指作品的名词于是也用来指研究这些作品的院系。

senses.title: Printed material used for promotion
senses.definition: leaflets, brochures and other printed matter used to advertise or explain something
senses.definitionCN: 用来宣传或说明某事的传单、小册子等印刷品
senses.example: The clinic sent promotional literature to every household.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所给每户人家都寄了宣传资料。
senses.why: Print carries authority, so advertisers borrowed the word for their brochures; a leaflet inherits the seriousness of a book even when it is selling soap.
senses.whyCN: 印刷品自带权威感，于是广告商借这个词来指自己的小册子；一张传单即便在推销肥皂，也继承了书本的严肃。

intro.en: Literature comes from a Latin word for writing and learning, and only later narrowed towards novels, poems and plays.
intro.cn: literature 来自拉丁语中表示书写与学问的词，后来才收窄到指小说、诗歌与戏剧。

items.en: Littera meant a letter of the alphabet, and the plural litterae often meant a written document or a letter sent to someone.
items.cn: littera 指字母表中的一个字母，复数 litterae 常指文书或寄给人的书信。

items.en: Litteratura named writing and the learning gained from letters, but not yet a shelf of novels.
items.cn: litteratura 指书写活动以及由文字得来的学问，那时还不指一整架小说。

items.en: Old French took the word as literature, still meaning learning and written culture rather than fiction.
items.cn: 古法语把这个词写作 literature，仍指学问与书面文化，而不是虚构故事。

items.en: Early English used literature for polite learning and scholarship; the modern sense of imaginative writing developed slowly.
items.cn: 早期英语用 literature 指文雅的学问与学术；指想象性写作的现代义项是慢慢发展出来的。

items.en: Modern English centres literature on novels, poems and plays, while keeping the older sense for the body of writing on any subject.
items.cn: 现代英语把 literature 的中心放在小说、诗歌与戏剧，同时保留较旧的义项，指任何主题的文献整体。

note.cn: 形近组沿着拉丁语中「字母、书写」的词干展开；近义组收表示故事、诗歌与文字作品的词。

normalIntro.en: The word grows out of the Latin word for a letter, and its family keeps returning to reading, learning and the works that carry both.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从拉丁语中表示「字母」的词生长出来，同族词反复回到阅读、学问以及承载二者的作品。

normal.en: Littera is a letter and litteratura is writing made of letters, so literature began as the product of the alphabet.
normal.cn: littera 是字母，litteratura 是由字母写成的文字，所以 literature 最初就是字母的产物。

normal.en: Literature first meant learning gained from books, which is why a literature review still means reading what others have written.
normal.cn: literature 最初指从书本得来的学问，所以文献综述至今仍指阅读别人已经写下的东西。

normal.en: Literary is the adjective and literature the noun: one describes, the other names the whole body of works.
normal.cn: literary 是形容词，literature 是名词：一个作描述，一个指整批作品。

normal.en: A field's literature is the shelf of everything written about it, which is why doctors speak of the literature on a drug.
normal.cn: 一个领域的 literature 就是关于它的全部书面材料，所以医生会说某种药的文献。

normal.en: Promotional literature borrows the prestige of books for leaflets, because print still looks authoritative.
normal.cn: 宣传资料借用了书本的声望来指传单，因为印刷品至今看起来仍然权威。

abstract.en: A library is many voices stored as letters, and literature is the name for that chorus.
abstract.cn: 图书馆是许多声音被存成字母，literature 就是这支合唱的名字。

abstract.en: The same word covers a tragedy and a clinic brochure, because both are printed and meant to be read.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指一部悲剧，也指诊所的小册子，因为两者都是印出来供人阅读的。

abstract.en: Literature is what a culture chooses to keep reading, and that choice changes with each generation.
abstract.cn: 文学是一个文化选择继续阅读的东西，而这个选择会随每一代人改变。

definition_zh: 活泼的；充满活力的；生动的；热闹的；鲜艳的；热烈的
definition_en: full of energy and enthusiasm, vivid and full of interest, busy with activity, bright in colour, or vigorous in argument
core_image: 一群孩子在院子里追着皮球跑，笑声把安静的午后掀了起来
scene: 午后的院子里，几个孩子追着皮球跑，笑声一阵接一阵。The lively children kept the whole street awake with their shouting.
sceneCN: 这里 lively 是「活泼的」（第 1 个义项：精力充沛、爱动）；句意为这些活泼的孩子用喊声让整条街都醒着。图中可辨识物件：院子、皮球、奔跑的孩子。

pos.zh: 活泼的；生动的；热闹的；鲜艳的；热烈的

senses.title: Full of energy and enthusiasm
senses.definition: full of energy, movement and enthusiasm, especially in the way a person or animal behaves
senses.definitionCN: 充满精力、动作与热情，尤指人或动物的举止
senses.example: The lively children kept the whole street awake with their shouting.
senses.exampleCN: 这些活泼的孩子用喊声让整条街都醒着。
senses.why: Old English liflic joins lif, life, to -lic, the suffix of likeness; the first sense is a creature visibly full of life, moving and making sound.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 liflic 把 lif（生命）与表示「像……一样」的后缀 -lic 连在一起；最早的义项就是看得见生命在动的活物，会跑会叫。

senses.title: Vivid and full of interest
senses.definition: vivid, interesting and full of imaginative detail, as in a lively description or a lively imagination
senses.definitionCN: 生动有趣、充满想象细节，如生动的描写或丰富的想象力
senses.example: She gave a lively account of the market on a rainy morning.
senses.exampleCN: 她把雨中清晨的集市讲得活灵活现。
senses.why: A description that keeps moving in the mind is felt to have life; the energy of a body is transferred to words, so a vivid account is called lively.
senses.whyCN: 一段在脑海里不断活动的描写会被觉得有生命；身体的能量转移到了文字上，于是生动的叙述就被称作 lively。

senses.title: Busy and full of activity
senses.definition: full of people, movement and excitement, as a place or an event
senses.definitionCN: 充满人群、动静与兴奋感，用来形容地方或活动
senses.example: The square becomes lively after the shops close.
senses.exampleCN: 商店打烊之后，广场就热闹起来。
senses.why: A crowd moves and makes noise like one large body; a place that will not stay quiet borrows the same word.
senses.whyCN: 人群又动又响，像一个巨大的身体；一个安静不下来的地方就借用了同一个词。

senses.title: Bright and strong in colour
senses.definition: of colour, bright and strong enough to catch the eye immediately
senses.definitionCN: 指颜色明亮强烈，一眼就能抓住视线
senses.example: The walls were painted a lively shade of orange.
senses.exampleCN: 墙壁被刷成一种鲜艳的橙色。
senses.why: Strong colour jumps at the eye the way a moving body does; the visual shock is read as a sign of life.
senses.whyCN: 浓烈的颜色像活动的身体一样跳进眼里；这种视觉冲击被读成生命力的标志。

senses.title: Vigorous and full of argument
senses.definition: of a discussion, debate or game, energetic and full of strong, differing views
senses.definitionCN: 指讨论、辩论或比赛充满劲头，带着强烈而不同的意见
senses.example: The proposal led to a lively debate in the council.
senses.exampleCN: 这项提议在议事会里引发了一场激烈的辩论。
senses.why: A debate that keeps returning and refuses to settle behaves like a restless creature; the energy of life is lent to argument.
senses.whyCN: 一场反复回到原点、不肯定论的辩论，举止就像一个停不下来的活物；生命的劲头被借给了争论。

intro.en: Lively began as a Germanic compound meaning life-like, and it gradually shifted from living creatures to vivid speech, bright colour and busy places.
intro.cn: lively 最初是一个意为「像生命一样的」日耳曼语复合词，后来逐渐从活物转到生动的言语、鲜亮的颜色和热闹的地方。

items.en: Old English liflic meant living or having life, built from lif, life, and the suffix -lic.
items.cn: 古英语 liflic 意为有生命的、活着的，由 lif（生命）与后缀 -lic 构成。

items.en: The noun is reconstructed as libam, the ancestor of life; the suffix -lic is related to German -lich and English -ly.
items.cn: 这个词的名词部分一般重构为 libam，是 life 的祖先；后缀 -lic 与德语 -lich、英语 -ly 同源。

items.en: Middle English lively kept the sense living and began to mean active, quick and cheerful.
items.cn: 中古英语的 lively 保留了「活着的」义项，并开始表示活跃、轻快、快活。

items.en: By the sixteenth century lively could describe vivid speech, bright colour and busy places, not only living creatures.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，lively 已能形容生动的言辞、鲜亮的颜色和热闹的地方，不再只用于活物。

items.en: Modern English uses lively mainly for energy and vividness; the older sense of living survives in a few fixed phrases such as a lively hope.
items.cn: 现代英语的 lively 主要用于表示活力与生动；较旧的「活着的」义项只留在少数固定说法里，如 a lively hope。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Germanic word for life; the near-meaning group gathers words for energy, vividness and busy activity.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在日耳曼语「生命」一词上的词；近义组收表示精力、生动与忙碌活动的词。

normalIntro.en: The word joins the Germanic noun for life to a suffix of likeness, and its family keeps returning to living energy and vivid movement.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把日耳曼语中表示「生命」的名词与表示「像……一样」的后缀结合起来，同族词反复回到活着的劲头与生动的动感。

normal.en: Old English liflic is life plus -lic, the suffix that became -ly; lively literally means life-like.
normal.cn: 古英语 liflic 是 life 加 -lic，也就是后来变成 -ly 的那个后缀；lively 字面上就是「像生命一样的」。

normal.en: The same suffix -ly appears in friendly and lovely, turning nouns into adjectives about a quality.
normal.cn: 同一个后缀 -ly 也出现在 friendly 与 lovely 里，把名词变成表示某种性质的形容词。

normal.en: Life, live and alive are close relatives, so a lively room is a room that seems to be alive.
normal.cn: life、live 与 alive 是近亲，所以一间 lively 的屋子就像一间活着的屋子。

normal.en: The word first described a living, moving body, and only later described speech, colour and markets.
normal.cn: 这个词最早描述会动会叫的活物，后来才用来描述言语、颜色和市场。

normal.en: Liveliness adds -ness to lively, naming the quality that a lively person or place shows.
normal.cn: liveliness 在 lively 后加 -ness，用来指活泼的人或地方所表现出的那种性质。

abstract.en: A lively room is one that behaves like a body: it moves, makes sound and will not sit still.
abstract.cn: 一间 lively 的屋子举止像个身体：会动、会响、不肯安静。

abstract.en: We call a description lively when reading it feels like watching something happen.
abstract.cn: 我们把一段描写称作 lively，是因为读它时像在看事情发生。

abstract.en: Bright colour and heated debate share the word because both refuse to stay quiet.
abstract.cn: 鲜艳的颜色与激烈的辩论共用这个词，因为两者都不肯安静。

definition_zh: 负荷；载荷；载重；负担；装载；加载
definition_en: the weight or force carried by a structure, vehicle or machine, or to put goods, data or a charge into something
core_image: 吊车把一卷钢带挂上吊钩，仪表指针逼近额定值，司机抬手示意停止起升
scene: 吊车把钢卷挂上吊钩，仪表指针逼近额定值，司机抬手示意停止起升。The crane stopped because the load exceeded its rated limit.
sceneCN: 这里指吊具承受的重量（第 1 个义项：结构或吊具承受的载荷）；句意为吊车停了下来，因为载荷超过了额定限度。图中可辨识物件：吊钩、钢卷、载荷仪表、司机、警戒线；对应第 1 个义项。

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「装料机；装载者」
由该动词加已然词尾构成，义为「载重的；有负载的」
由该动词加表示进行的名词尾构成，义为「装载；加载」
由表示「超过」的前缀加该词构成，义为「超载」
由表示「取消」的前缀加该动词构成，义为「卸载」

senses.title: The weight a structure carries
senses.definition: the force or weight that a structure, lifting device or machine has to bear
senses.definitionCN: 结构、吊具或机器必须承受的力或重量
senses.example: The beam is designed for a load of ten tonnes.
senses.exampleCN: 这根梁按十吨载荷设计。
senses.why: The word began as a way or a carrying, and engineering fixed it to the weight being carried.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指「路途、承载」，工程语境把它固定到被承载的重量上。

senses.title: The capacity of a vehicle
senses.definition: the amount of goods or weight that a vehicle or vessel is able to carry
senses.definitionCN: 车辆或船舶能够装载的货物量或重量
senses.example: The truck took a full load of gravel.
senses.exampleCN: 卡车装了一整载碎石。
senses.why: A carrying word naturally measures how much can be carried at once.
senses.whyCN: 表示「承载」的词自然用来度量一次能带多少。

senses.title: The weight of work
senses.definition: the amount of work or responsibility a person or system must deal with
senses.definitionCN: 一个人或系统必须处理的工作量或责任
senses.example: The new clerk cut the load on the front desk.
senses.exampleCN: 新来的职员减轻了前台的负担。
senses.why: Work is imagined as goods to be carried, and an extra person shares the load.
senses.whyCN: 工作被想象成要搬运的货物，多一个人就分担了荷载。

senses.title: The demand on a circuit
senses.definition: the power or current drawn by a device or system from a supply
senses.definitionCN: 设备或系统从电源取用的功率或电流
senses.example: The generator tripped when the load doubled.
senses.exampleCN: 负载翻倍时发电机跳闸了。
senses.why: Electrical demand behaves like a weight on a supply, and the old word fitted without change.
senses.whyCN: 用电需求像压在电源上的重量，老词原样就用上了。

senses.title: To put goods on board
senses.definition: to put goods, fuel or material onto a vehicle or into a container
senses.definitionCN: 把货物、燃料或材料放上车船或容器
senses.example: They load the pallets before sunrise.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在日出前把托盘装好。
senses.why: The noun of a burden turned into the verb of placing it, a common British pairing.
senses.whyCN: 「负担」的名词转成「放置负担」的动词，这是英语里常见的名词动化。

senses.title: To charge a weapon or device
senses.definition: to put a charge, film or medium into a weapon, camera or appliance
senses.definitionCN: 把弹药、胶片或介质装入武器、相机或器具
senses.example: He loaded the camera with a fresh roll.
senses.exampleCN: 他给相机装上一卷新胶卷。
senses.why: A device also carries something and needs to be filled before it works.
senses.whyCN: 装置同样要承载东西，用之前必须先填满。

senses.title: To bring data into memory
senses.definition: to transfer a file or program into a computer's memory so that it can be used
senses.definitionCN: 把文件或程序传入计算机内存以便使用
senses.example: The program will load the map on startup.
senses.exampleCN: 程序启动时会加载这张地图。
senses.why: Computing reused the idea of putting something into a carrier before it can act.
senses.whyCN: 计算机沿用「先装进载体才能运作」这个思路。

senses.title: An emotional burden
senses.definition: a weight of worry or responsibility that a person feels
senses.definitionCN: 一个人感受到的忧虑或责任之重
senses.example: She carried a heavy load after the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 事故之后她背负着沉重的心理负担。
senses.why: The body carries weight and the mind borrows the same measure.
senses.whyCN: 身体承担重量，心智借用了同一套度量。

senses.title: The demand on an engine
senses.definition: the amount of power an engine or motor must produce at a given moment
senses.definitionCN: 发动机或电动机在某一时刻必须输出的功率
senses.example: At full load the engine runs at its hottest.
senses.exampleCN: 满负荷时发动机温度最高。
senses.why: Every machine has a working demand, and engineers call that demand its load.
senses.whyCN: 每台机器都有运转需求，工程师把这个需求称作它的负荷。

intro.en: Load goes back to Old English lad, a way or a course, from the reconstructed Proto-Germanic laidō, to go forth. The sense of something carried appeared in Middle English, and the verb followed.
intro.cn: 这个词可追到古英语 lad「路途、进程」，来自原始日耳曼语的重构形式 laidō「向前走」。表示「被承载之物」的意思在中古英语出现，动词随后产生。

items.en: Lad meant a way, a course or a journey, and the earliest sense was about travelling rather than weight.
items.cn: 这个词意为路途、进程或旅程，最早的意思与行走有关，而非重量。

items.en: The Proto-Germanic noun meant a way or a leading, and related forms in other Germanic languages also mean a road or a track.
items.cn: 原始日耳曼语名词意为路途或引导，其他日耳曼语中的相关形式也指道路或轨迹。

items.en: By the thirteenth century the word also named what a person or animal carried, and the meaning moved from route to burden; how that shift came about is source uncertain, and one hypothesis links it to a related verb meaning to lead.
items.cn: 到十三世纪，这个词也指人或牲畜背负的东西，意思从路线转向负担；这一语义转变的来源不确定，另有假说认为它受表示「引导、带领」的同族动词影响。

items.en: The verb to put a load on appeared in the fourteenth century, and to load a gun or camera followed later.
items.cn: 表示「给……装货」的动词在十四世纪出现，给枪炮或相机装填的用法随后产生。

items.en: Structural and mechanical engineering gave the noun its precise force sense, and its first attestation date is uncertain.
items.cn: 结构与机械工程赋予这个名词精确的力学含义，首见年代不确定。

items.en: The nineteenth century applied the word to circuits, and the twentieth to data and programs.
items.cn: 十九世纪把它用于电路，二十世纪又用于数据与程序。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like load; the second group names neighbouring ideas of weight and filling.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与「load」相近；第二组是与「重量、装载」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: A machine or person that loads material, or a program that loads files.
entries.definitionCN: 指装料的机器或人，也指加载文件的程序。

entries.definition: Carrying a load, or charged with something.
entries.definitionCN: 指载着负荷的，或装填了东西的。

entries.definition: To put more weight or demand on something than it can bear.
entries.definitionCN: 指给某物加上超过其承受能力的重量或需求。

entries.definition: To take goods off a vehicle or remove a burden.
entries.definitionCN: 指把货物从车上卸下或卸去负担。

entries.definition: A vein of ore; it sounds identical but comes from a word for a way or a lead.
entries.definitionCN: 指矿脉；发音相同，但来自表示「路径、引导」的词。

entries.definition: A heavy load, especially one that is hard to carry or bear.
entries.definitionCN: 指沉重的负荷，尤指难以承担的重负。

entries.definition: The heaviness of an object, or a mass placed on something.
entries.definitionCN: 指物体的重量，或放在某物上的质量。

entries.definition: Goods carried by a ship, aircraft or truck.
entries.definitionCN: 指船、飞机或卡车运载的货物。

entries.definition: The part of a vehicle's load that earns revenue or does the work.
entries.definitionCN: 指载具负荷中产生收益或执行任务的那部分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real way-word origin, the real trade family and real engineering phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「路途」来源、真实行业同族词与真实工程搭配。

normal.en: Load first meant a road, then the thing a road carries.
normal.cn: load 最初指一条路，后来指这条路所承载的东西。

normal.en: Load capacity and heavy load are the engineering phrases.
normal.cn: 承载能力与重载是工程里的说法。

normal.en: Load a truck, load a camera and load data are three filling acts.
normal.cn: 装车、装胶卷与加载数据是三个「装填」动作。

normal.en: Overload and unload mark too much and none at all.
normal.cn: 超载与卸载标出「太多」与「一点不剩」。

normal.en: Workload is the same weight carried by a person rather than a beam.
normal.cn: 工作量就是由人而不是梁来承担的同一份重量。

abstract.en: A load is a promise the structure must keep every second.
abstract.cn: 载荷是结构每一秒都必须守住的承诺。

abstract.en: The same word weighs a steel coil and a bad memory.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既称钢卷的重量，也称一段坏记忆的重量。

abstract.en: Loading is putting something in so that the thing can begin.
abstract.cn: 加载就是把东西放进去，好让那件事得以开始。

examples.en: The column carries the load of the roof above it.
examples.cn: 这根柱子承受上方屋顶的载荷。

examples.en: Workers load the truck before the gate opens.
examples.cn: 工人在大门打开前装车。

examples.en: The screen froze while the program was loading the file.
examples.cn: 程序加载文件时屏幕卡住了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「漏德」——压在梁上的重量不能「漏」掉，得全「德」扛住：负荷

root: 古英语 lad「路途、进程」← 原始日耳曼语 laidō「向前走」；同族形式多指道路或轨迹。十三世纪起转指所背负之物，十四世纪产生动词，十五世纪用于枪炮装填，十九世纪用于电路，二十世纪用于数据；力学义的确切年代来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all concern what is carried: force on a structure, goods in a vehicle, work on a person, current in a circuit, cargo placed on board, a charge in a device, data in memory, worry in a mind, and power drawn from an engine.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都与「承载」有关：结构受力、车辆载货、人的工作量、电路电流、装船装车、装置装填、内存数据、心中忧虑与发动机输出功率。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hook lifts a coil until the gauge reaches the rated limit.
core.cn: 核心意象：吊钩吊起钢卷，直到仪表到达额定极限。

branches.en: THE FORCE ON A MACHINE: a beam bearing tonnes, and an engine working at full demand.
branches.cn: 机器所受的力：梁承受数吨重量，发动机满负荷运转。

branches.en: THE CARGO: the amount a vehicle can take, and the act of putting it aboard.
branches.cn: 货物：车辆能装的数量，以及把货装上去的动作。

branches.en: THE HUMAN WEIGHT: too much work at a desk, and too much worry in a mind.
branches.cn: 人的重量：桌上过多的工作，与心中过多的忧虑。

branches.en: THE ELECTRICAL DRAW: current taken from a supply until the breaker trips.
branches.cn: 电的取用：从电源取用电流，直到断路器跳闸。

branches.en: THE THING PUT IN: a charge in a weapon, and a file brought into memory.
branches.cn: 装进去的东西：装进武器的弹药，以及带进内存的文件。

intro.en: Load is a native English word of Germanic origin, so it has no Latin ancestor; its Latin list is left empty.
intro.cn: 这是一个日耳曼来源的英语本族词，没有拉丁语祖先，因此拉丁词条留空。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source for load; the relevant origin is Proto-Germanic laidō, a word for a way or a course.
latinIntro.cn: load 没有拉丁语来源；相关来源是原始日耳曼语 laidō，指路途或进程。

items.example: The oldest sense is about moving, not carrying.
items.exampleCN: 最古老的意思关乎行走，而非承载。

items.example: The form is reconstructed from related languages.
items.exampleCN: 该形式由相关语言重构而来。

items.example: It forms the adjective loaded.
It forms the noun loading.
It forms loader.
It forms overload.
It forms unload.
The compound moves the load from steel to people.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词把负荷从钢梁转到人身上。

items.meaning: the earning part of a load
items.meaningCN: 负荷中产生收益的部分
items.example: The compound separates cargo from the vehicle.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词把货物与载具分开。

由该动词加表示进行的名词尾构成，义为「装载；加载」

definition_zh: 贷款；借款；出借；借用物；借词
definition_en: money lent on the understanding that it will be repaid, or any thing lent for temporary use
core_image: 一只手把一叠钱推过桌面，桌对面的人签下一张写有归还日期的纸
scene: 年底，小店老板在银行签下文件，拿到一笔钱用于进货，约定按月归还。The shop took out a loan to buy stock for the winter.
sceneCN: 这里 loan 指「贷款」（第 1 个义项：借出并约定归还的钱）；句意为这家小店取得一笔贷款来备冬季存货。图中可辨识物件：合同、钞票、日历、签字笔；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 贷款；借款；借用物；借词（可数）

derivatives.zh: 借出；贷款给
出借人；放贷方

senses.title: Money lent for repayment
senses.definition: a sum of money given to a borrower on condition that it is paid back, usually with interest
senses.definitionCN: 交给借款人、约定归还（通常附利息）的一笔钱
senses.example: The shop took out a loan to buy stock for the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 这家小店取得一笔贷款来备冬季存货。
senses.why: the core of the word is a thing handed over temporarily, and money is the thing most often handed over on those terms.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的核心是临时交出的东西，而钱是最常按这种条件交出的东西。

senses.title: The act of lending
senses.definition: the act or arrangement of lending something, as in the making of a loan
senses.definitionCN: 借出某物的行为或安排，如放贷
senses.example: The loan was arranged in a single afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔贷款在一个下午就办妥了。
senses.why: English uses the same noun for the act and the object, so a loan can name the transaction as well as the sum.
senses.whyCN: 英语用同一个名词指行为和物件，因此 loan 既可指交易，也可指金额。

senses.title: An object lent temporarily
senses.definition: a thing other than money lent for temporary use, such as a book or a tool
senses.definitionCN: 除金钱外临时借出的物品，如书或工具
senses.example: The library made a loan of the atlas for one week.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆把地图册外借一周。
senses.why: the money sense is the dominant one, but the older general sense of a thing lent never disappeared.
senses.whyCN: 金钱义占主导，但「借出之物」这一更早的泛指义从未消失。

senses.title: A word borrowed from another language
senses.definition: a word taken into one language from another, usually shortened from loanword
senses.definitionCN: 从另一种语言进入某种语言的词，通常是 loanword 的缩略
senses.example: Sushi is a loan in English from Japanese.
senses.exampleCN: sushi 是英语从日语借来的借词。
senses.why: linguists extended the money metaphor to words, which are borrowed and never returned.
senses.whyCN: 语言学家把金钱比喻扩展到词上：词被借走，却从不归还。

senses.title: To lend, as a verb
senses.definition: to give something to someone for temporary use, especially in American usage
senses.definitionCN: 把某物交给他人临时使用，尤见于美式用法
senses.example: The bank loaned the money at a fixed rate.
senses.exampleCN: 银行以固定利率贷出这笔钱。
senses.why: the verb is a later back-formation from the noun and remains less common than lend in British English.
senses.whyCN: 动词义是从名词后起的逆构，在英式英语中仍不如 lend 常用。

senses.title: A temporarily transferred player
senses.definition: in sport, a player allowed to play for another club for a period while still under contract
senses.definitionCN: 体育中仍在原俱乐部合同期内、被允许为另一俱乐部短期出赛的球员
senses.example: The young striker joined on loan until June.
senses.exampleCN: 这名年轻前锋以租借形式加盟到六月。
senses.why: a player is the object lent: the owning club keeps the contract, the other club gets temporary use.
senses.whyCN: 球员就是被借出的对象：原俱乐部保留合同，另一俱乐部获得临时使用权。

senses.title: A work lent for an exhibition
senses.definition: a painting or object lent by one museum to another for a show
senses.definitionCN: 一家博物馆借给另一家用于展览的画作或器物
senses.example: The portrait is a loan from a private collection.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅肖像是从私人收藏借展的作品。
senses.why: museums use the word because ownership stays put while the object travels temporarily.
senses.whyCN: 博物馆用这个词，因为物件临时出门而所有权留在原处。

senses.title: A temporary grant, figuratively
senses.definition: a short grant of something immaterial, such as time, attention or confidence
senses.definitionCN: 对无形之物的短期给予，如时间、关注或信心
senses.example: Time is a generous lender of second chances.
senses.exampleCN: 时间总是大方地借出重来的机会。
senses.why: the metaphor treats time and trust as things lent rather than given, since they must be returned in some form.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把时间与信任当作借出而非给出之物，因为它们终须以某种形式归还。

intro.en: Loan is a Scandinavian borrowing into English, not a Latin word. It is closely tied to lend, and the two descend from one Germanic idea. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: loan 是英语从斯堪的纳维亚语借入的词，并非拉丁词。它与 lend 关系密切，两者源自同一个日耳曼概念。年代均为约数。

items.en: Old Norse lán meant 'loan, something lent'; it entered English during the Viking settlements and settled into the everyday vocabulary.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 lán 意为「借款、被借出之物」，在维京人定居时期进入英语，并落入日常词汇。

items.en: Old English had læn 'loan' and lænan 'to lend'; the native noun was later replaced in most uses by the Scandinavian form.
items.cn: 古英语有 læn「借款」与 lænan「借出」；本族名词后来在多数用法中被斯堪的纳维亚形式取代。

items.en: The Germanic stock is generally traced to a root meaning 'to leave', so that a loan is literally something left with another person.
items.cn: 这套日耳曼词一般被追溯到表示「留下」的词根，因此借款字面上就是留在别人手里的东西。

items.en: That root would make loan a distant relative of Latin linquere 'to leave', but the connection is a reconstruction and not a borrowing from Latin.
items.cn: 若该词根成立，loan 便是拉丁 linquere「留下」的远亲；但这一联系属重构形式，并非从拉丁语借入。

items.en: Middle English wrote the word as lone or lane; the modern spelling with -oa- is a later convention.
items.cn: 中世纪英语把这个词写作 lone 或 lane；现代带 -oa- 的拼法是后来的惯例。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the exact first record in English is not fixed, and the pre-Germanic root is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：它在英语中的最早记录没有定论，日耳曼语之前的词根属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds forms that share the lending stem; group two holds financial words that overlap with loan but differ in who owes and who owns.
note.cn: 第一组是共用「借出」词干的形式；第二组是与 loan 重叠、但在「谁欠谁、谁拥有」上不同的金融词。

entries.definition: The native verb for giving something temporarily; loan as a verb is its American twin.
entries.definitionCN: 本族动词，表示临时给出；作动词的 loan 是它的美式孪生形式。

entries.definition: One who lends; the ending -er marks the giver, not the thing given.
entries.definitionCN: 出借的人；词尾 -er 标记给予者，而非被给予之物。

entries.definition: The person who receives a loan; -ee marks the receiver, the mirror of -er.
entries.definitionCN: 接受贷款的人；-ee 标记接受者，与 -er 相对。

entries.definition: Meaning 'solitary', from a different stem; it sounds exactly like loan but shares no history.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「孤单的」，词干不同；读音与 loan 完全相同，却无共同来源。

entries.definition: The trust that allows goods or money to be given before payment; a loan is the sum so given.
entries.definitionCN: 允许先给货或钱后付款的信任；loan 是据此给出的款项。

entries.definition: A loan secured on property; it is one kind of loan, not a synonym for all loans.
entries.definitionCN: 以财产作担保的贷款；是贷款的一种，并非所有贷款的统称。

entries.definition: The obligation created by a loan; the loan is the money handed over, the debt is what remains owed.
entries.definitionCN: 贷款产生的偿付义务；loan 是交出的钱，debt 是仍欠的部分。

entries.definition: Money paid before it is due, often to a worker or supplier; it may or may not be repaid.
entries.definitionCN: 在到期前支付的款项，常给工人或供应商；可能需偿还，也可能不必。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Loan came from Old Norse, and lend is its native English cousin from the same Germanic idea.
normal.cn: loan 来自古诺斯语，lend 是同一日耳曼概念下的英语本族表亲。

normal.en: The family runs loan, lend, lender, loanee, loanable, loanword and reloan.
normal.cn: 同族包括 loan、lend、lender、loanee、loanable、loanword 与 reloan。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: take out a loan, pay off a loan, a student loan, on loan.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：取得贷款、还清贷款、学生贷款、借来的。

normal.en: Loan and lone sound alike but have no shared history.
normal.cn: loan 与 lone 读音相同，却没有共同来源。

normal.en: Museums and football clubs both say on loan when ownership stays put.
normal.cn: 博物馆与足球俱乐部都用 on loan，表示所有权留在原处。

abstract.en: Picture a coin handed across a table with a string still tied to the giver's hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币递过桌面，绳子的另一端仍系在给出者手上。

abstract.en: Picture a borrowed book that returns with someone else's notes in the margin.
abstract.cn: 想象一本借出的书回来时页边写着别人的批注。

abstract.en: Picture time as a bank that lends hours and asks for them back later.
abstract.cn: 想象时间是一家银行，借出小时，日后又要求归还。

examples.en: The loan must be repaid within five years.
examples.cn: 这笔贷款必须在五年内归还。

examples.en: She took the novel on loan from the library.
examples.cn: 她从图书馆借走了那本小说。

examples.en: The painting is on loan to the museum for the summer.
examples.cn: 这幅画整个夏天借展给博物馆。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「loan 借出」——钱借出去，约期归还 → 贷款、借用物

root: 古诺斯语 lán「借款、借出之物」，与古英语 læn、动词 lænan「借出」同源；这套词一般追溯到表示「留下」的日耳曼词根，与拉丁 linquere「留下」的更深联系属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act: something is handed over for temporary use and must come back, whether money, a book, a player, a painting, a word or a little time.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：把某物交出供临时使用，并终须归还，无论那是钱、书、球员、画作、词，还是一点时间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coin pushed across a table with a string still tied to the giver.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚硬币被推过桌面，绳子的另一端仍系在给出者手上。

branches.en: MONEY AND ITS ACT: the sum lent and the transaction share one noun.
branches.cn: 钱与行为：借出的金额与这笔交易共用一个名词。

branches.en: OBJECTS THAT TRAVEL: a book or a painting leaves its owner for a while and returns.
branches.cn: 出门的物件：书或画暂时离开主人，然后再回来。

branches.en: WORDS THAT NEVER RETURN: a borrowed word stays in the new language for good.
branches.cn: 不再归还的词：借词永久留在新语言里。

branches.en: THE VERB FORM: the same transaction seen as an action rather than a thing.
branches.cn: 动词形式：同一笔交易被看作动作而非物件。

branches.en: TEMPORARY GRANTS: a player and a stretch of time are both lent without being given away.
branches.cn: 暂时的给予：球员与一段时间都是借出，而非送出。

intro.en: Loan is a whole Scandinavian word, so its family is built by adding English endings to loan or to its native twin lend, not by peeling off Latin parts.
intro.cn: loan 是一个完整的斯堪的纳维亚词，因此它的词族靠给 loan 或其本族孪生词 lend 加英语词尾构成，而不是拆拉丁成分。

latinIntro.en: No Latin word stands behind loan; Latin expressed the idea with mutuum, which is not related in form. Any link through the root for 'leave' is a reconstruction at a deeper level.
latinIntro.cn: loan 背后没有拉丁词；拉丁语用 mutuum 表达这一概念，而它在形式上并无关联。通过「留下」词根建立的联系属更深层的重构形式。

items.example: The loan runs for three years.
They lend tools to their neighbours.
The lender set a fixed rate.
The loanee signed the schedule.
Only loanable stock leaves the store.
items.exampleCN: 只有可出借的库存才会离开商店。

items.meaning: a word taken from another language
items.example: The dictionary marks each loanword.

items.meaning: to lend again or pass on a loan
items.example: The bank reloaned the repaid funds.
items.exampleCN: 银行把已还的资金再次贷出。

definition_zh: 当地的；本地的；局部的；本地人；住处附近的酒吧；每站都停的慢车
definition_en: relating to a particular area or neighbourhood, affecting only one part of the body, a person who lives nearby, the pub nearest one's home, or a train that stops at every station
core_image: 街角一家小店的木牌上写着本街的名字，推门进去的人多半互相认识
scene: 周末的集市上，摊主把自家菜园刚摘的蔬菜摆上木桌，牌子上写着村子的名字。We bought honey from a local farmer at the market.
sceneCN: 这里 local 是「当地的」（第 1 个义项：属于某一地方的）；句意为我们在集市上从一位当地农夫那里买了蜂蜜。图中可辨识物件：木桌、菜蔬、写着村名的木牌。

pos.zh: 本地人；住处附近的酒吧；慢车

senses.title: Belonging to a particular area
senses.definition: belonging to or connected with a particular small area, town or neighbourhood
senses.definitionCN: 属于或与某一小片区域、城镇或街区有关的
senses.example: We bought honey from a local farmer at the market.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在集市上从一位当地农夫那里买了蜂蜜。
senses.why: Latin locus means place, and the adjective built on it simply marks whatever belongs to one place rather than to the whole country.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 locus 意为「地方」，由它构成的形容词只是标记某物属于某一处，而不是属于整个国家。

senses.title: A person who lives in the area
senses.definition: a person who lives in a particular area, especially as opposed to a visitor
senses.definitionCN: 住在某一地区的人，尤指相对于外来访客而言
senses.example: The locals were friendly and pointed us towards the old bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 当地人都很友善，还给我们指了去老桥的路。
senses.why: If an adjective can label anything of a place, it can stand alone as a name for the people of that place, so the adjective turned into a countable noun.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个形容词能标记属于某地的一切，它就能单独出来指那个地方的人，于是形容词变成了可数名词。

senses.title: The pub nearest one's home
senses.definition: in British informal speech, the pub close to where one lives and goes regularly
senses.definitionCN: 英式非正式说法，指住家附近、常去的那家酒吧
senses.example: We spent the evening at our local, talking to the barman.
senses.exampleCN: 我们晚上待在住处附近那家酒吧，和酒保聊天。
senses.why: British drinkers shorten the phrase the local pub to the local, so the adjective absorbs its noun and becomes a familiar place with a definite article.
senses.whyCN: 英国喝酒的人把 the local pub 缩成 the local，形容词吞掉了它修饰的名词，成了一个带定冠词的熟悉去处。

senses.title: Affecting only one part of the body
senses.definition: affecting only a small area of the body rather than the whole of it
senses.definitionCN: 只影响身体的一小块区域，而不是全身
senses.example: The dentist gave her a local anaesthetic before drilling.
senses.exampleCN: 牙医在钻牙之前给她用了局部麻醉。
senses.why: Medicine needed a word for treatment confined to one spot, and the adjective for belonging to a place was ready to mark a boundary inside the body.
senses.whyCN: 医学需要一个词来表示只限于某一处的治疗，而那个表示「属于某地」的形容词正好能在身体内部划出边界。

senses.title: A train that stops at every station
senses.definition: a train or bus that stops at every station along its route, in American usage
senses.definitionCN: 美式用法中指沿途每站都停的火车或公共汽车
senses.example: He took the local instead of the express and watched the small towns go by.
senses.exampleCN: 他坐了慢车而不是快车，一路上看着小镇慢慢退后。
senses.why: Railway timetables contrasted the express with the train serving each locality, and the name of the small place became the name of the slow service.
senses.whyCN: 铁路时刻表把快车与逐站服务各处的车对立起来，于是「小地方」的名字成了慢车的名字。

intro.en: Local goes back to the Latin word for place; the adjective travelled through French and then grew noun uses for people, pubs and trains.
intro.cn: local 可一直追到拉丁语中表示「地方」的词；这个形容词经法语进入英语，后来又长出指人、指酒吧和指慢车的名词用法。

items.en: Locus was the ordinary Latin noun for a place or a position, and its verb locare meant to put something in a place.
items.cn: locus 是拉丁语中表示地方或位置的普通名词，它的动词 locare 意为把某物放到某处。

items.en: Medieval Latin formed localis for whatever belongs to a particular place, and the adjective carried that narrow sense forward.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语造出 localis，指属于某一特定地方的东西，这个形容词把这层狭窄的意思继续传下去。

items.en: Old French used local as an adjective of place, and English borrowed it in the late fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语用 local 作为表示地方的形容词，英语在十四世纪晚期把它借了过来。

items.en: English applied local to parishes, customs and news, and in the nineteenth century began using it as a noun for the people and services of a place.
items.cn: 英语把 local 用于教区、习俗与新闻，并在十九世纪开始把它当名词，指一地的人和设施。

items.en: Modern English keeps local for the neighbourhood, medicine for a limited area of the body, British speech for the nearby pub, and American timetables for the stopping train.
items.cn: 现代英语用 local 指邻里，医学用它指身体的局部，英式口语用它指附近的酒吧，美式时刻表用它指逐站停靠的慢车。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers relatives built on the Latin word for place; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives that also mark where something belongs.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「地方」一词上的同族词；近义组收同样标记归属范围的形容词。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on the Latin noun for place, and its family keeps returning to position, neighbourhood and the services of one small area.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语表示「地方」的名词上，它的同族词反复回到位置、邻里，以及某一小片区域的设施。

normal.en: Latin locus means place, so local is literally the adjective of a place, not of a whole country.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 locus 意为地方，所以 local 字面就是「属于某地的」形容词，而不是属于整个国家的。

normal.en: Locality adds -ity to local and names the area itself, while locate returns to the Latin verb for placing.
normal.cn: locality 在 local 后加 -ity，直接指那片区域；locate 则回到拉丁语中表示「放置」的动词。

normal.en: Local time is the time of one meridian, which is why a flight announcement always names it.
normal.cn: local time 是某一条经线上的时间，所以航班广播总要说明是当地时间。

normal.en: British speakers call their regular pub the local, shortening the local pub to one familiar word.
normal.cn: 英国人说 the local 指自己常去的酒吧，把 the local pub 缩成一个熟悉的词。

normal.en: A local train stops at each locality, so the adjective for small places became a noun for slow service.
normal.cn: local train 在每一个小地方都停，于是「小地方」的形容词变成了慢车的名词。

abstract.en: One adjective for place can name the people, the pub and the train, because all three are defined by being near.
abstract.cn: 同一个表示地方的形容词能指人、指酒吧、指火车，因为这三者都由「近」来定义。

abstract.en: Local and regional both answer where, but local draws a much smaller circle around the speaker.
abstract.cn: local 与 regional 都在回答「在哪里」，但 local 在说话者周围画出的圈小得多。

abstract.en: Medicine borrows the word to draw a border inside the body, showing how a place word can be used for any limited area.
abstract.cn: 医学借这个词在身体内部划一条边界，说明一个表示地方的词可用于任何有限的范围。

definition_zh: 找出……的位置；位于；安置；设立；定位
definition_en: to find the exact position of something, to place it in a position, or to be situated in a place
core_image: 一张摊开的地图上，一枚图钉被按在某个精确的坐标点上
scene: 维修员戴上耳机，用测漏仪贴着墙面慢慢移动。The needle jumped near the bathroom wall, and that was enough to locate the broken pipe behind the tiles.
sceneCN: 这里 locate 是「找出确切位置」（第 1 个义项：确定某物的位置）；句意：指针在浴室墙边突然跳动，这样就足以找出瓷砖后面那截破裂的水管。图中可辨识物件：测漏仪、耳机、墙面记号、水管剖面图；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 找出……的位置；使坐落于；安置；设立
位于；定居（多用于 be located）

位于……的；坐落于……的
定位器；定位装置

senses.title: Find the exact position of something
senses.definition: to discover the exact place where someone or something is
senses.definitionCN: 发现某人或某物所在的确切地点
senses.example: Rescuers used heat sensors to locate the trapped climbers.
senses.exampleCN: 救援人员用热传感器找到了受困登山者的位置。
senses.why: Latin locare meant 'to place', and locus meant 'place'. The modern verb starts by finding the place that belongs to a person or object: the pin is put back on the map.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 locare 意为“放置”，locus 意为“地点”。现代动词的起点是找到某人或某物所属的那个地点：把图钉重新按回地图上。

senses.title: Be situated: occupy a place
senses.definition: in the passive be located, to be situated in a particular place
senses.definitionCN: 用于被动式 be located，表示位于某个特定地点
senses.example: The laboratory is located on the third floor.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室位于三楼。
senses.why: Once a thing has been placed, the result of that placing is a position. English prefers the passive be located for this state, because the place, not the placer, is what matters.
senses.whyCN: 某物被放置之后，放置的结果就是一个位置。英语用被动式 be located 表达这种状态，因为重要的是地点，而不是放置者。

senses.title: Place something deliberately
senses.titleCN: 安置：有意把某物放在某处
senses.definition: to put or fix something in a particular position, especially as part of a plan
senses.definitionCN: 把某物放置或固定在特定位置，尤作为计划的一部分
senses.example: Engineers located the sensor where the pipe bends.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师把传感器安置在管道弯曲处。
senses.why: This sense returns to the Latin verb's active core: locare is to place. The object is not merely found but deliberately given a position.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项回到拉丁动词的主动核心：locare 就是放置。对象不是被找到，而是被有意赋予一个位置。

senses.title: Establish a business or branch in a place
senses.titleCN: 设立：把机构或分支落户某地
senses.definition: to establish an office, factory, or organization in a particular place
senses.definitionCN: 在某地设立办事处、工厂或组织
senses.example: The company located its regional office near the port.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司把地区办事处设在港口附近。
senses.why: A business chooses a place and then settles there. The verb shifts from a single object to an institution that occupies a site, a common use in commerce and planning.
senses.whyCN: 企业先选择一个地点，然后在那里落脚。动词的宾语从单个物件变成占据场地的机构，这是商业与规划中的常见用法。

senses.title: Pinpoint a fault or cause
senses.titleCN: 确定故障或问题的所在
senses.definition: to identify the exact source of a problem, fault, or pain
senses.definitionCN: 确定问题、故障或疼痛的确切来源
senses.example: The technician located the fault in a single connector.
senses.exampleCN: 技术员把故障定位到一个连接器上。
senses.why: A fault is invisible until it is assigned to a point. Locating it means narrowing the search until one place on the system carries the explanation.
senses.whyCN: 故障在被指认到某个点之前是不可见的。定位故障，就是把搜索范围收窄，直到系统上的某一处承载了解释。

senses.title: Technical positioning: radar, sonar, GPS
senses.titleCN: 技术定位：雷达、声呐与全球定位
senses.definition: to determine the position of an object or signal using an instrument
senses.definitionCN: 用仪器确定物体或信号的位置
senses.example: The system locates the drone within ten metres.
senses.exampleCN: 该系统能把无人机定位在十米范围内。
senses.why: Instruments extend the search: a signal is sent, an echo returns, and the delay is converted into coordinates. The old 'place' is now a mathematical point in space.
senses.whyCN: 仪器延伸了搜索：发出信号、收到回波，再把延迟换算成坐标。原来的“地点”如今成了空间中的数学点。

senses.title: Find a passage inside a larger whole
senses.definition: to find a particular passage, file, or item within a larger document or system
senses.definitionCN: 在较大的文档或系统中找到特定段落、文件或条目
senses.example: She located the relevant paragraph in the online manual.
senses.exampleCN: 她在在线手册中找到了相关段落。
senses.why: The 'map' can be a book, a database, or a filing system. Locating is not discovering a new thing but putting your finger on the known place where it sits.
senses.whyCN: 这里的“地图”可以是书、数据库或档案系统。定位不是发现新东西，而是把手指按到它已知所在的那个位置。

senses.title: Map a gene to a chromosome
senses.titleCN: 基因定位：把基因标到染色体上
senses.definition: in genetics, to determine the position of a gene or sequence on a chromosome
senses.definitionCN: 在遗传学中，确定基因或序列在染色体上的位置
senses.example: The team located the mutation on the long arm of chromosome 7.
senses.exampleCN: 团队把该突变定位在 7 号染色体的长臂上。
senses.why: A chromosome is a linear map, and a gene has an address on it. This specialist sense applies the same 'find its place' structure to molecular coordinates.
senses.whyCN: 染色体是一张线性的地图，基因在上面有地址。这个专业义项把同样的“找到它的位置”结构用于分子坐标。

senses.title: Usage boundary: pinpoint, not merely encounter
senses.titleCN: 用法边界：强调精确定位，而非偶然遇到
senses.definition: a usage limit: locate stresses an exact position; find is broader, and be located describes a state rather than an action
senses.definitionCN: 用法限制：locate 强调确切位置；find 范围更宽；be located 描述状态而不是动作
senses.example: I found an old letter in the drawer, but I could not locate the address on any map.
senses.exampleCN: 我在抽屉里发现一封旧信，却无法在任何地图上确定那个地址的位置。
senses.why: Finding can be accidental and can concern anything; locating requires a position that can be specified. The passive state also blocks the progressive in ordinary description, so 'is located' replaces 'is locating'.
senses.whyCN: find 可以是偶然的，也可以针对任何东西；locate 则要求一个能被指明的位置。被动状态在通常描述中也不用进行体，因此用 is located 而不是 is locating。

intro.en: Locate comes from Latin locus 'place' through the verb locare 'to place'. The English verb is early modern, while the 'find the position' sense is much later. The deeper origin of locus is uncertain.
intro.cn: locate 经由拉丁动词 locare“放置”来自拉丁名词 locus“地点”。英语动词出现于近代早期，而“找出位置”的义项要晚得多。locus 更深层的来源并不确定。

items.en: Latin locus meant 'a place, spot, position'. It also developed the sense 'passage in a book', because a text is a kind of place one visits. Its deeper PIE origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 拉丁语 locus 意为“地点、位置”，还发展出“书中的段落”义，因为文本也是一种可以被造访的地方。它更深的原始印欧语来源不确定。

items.en: From locus came locare 'to place, put, set'. The verb also meant 'to let out for hire', which survives in the leasing sense of location in some languages.
items.cn: 由 locus 产生 locare“放置、安放”。这个动词还表示“出租”，这一义项在一些语言中保留在 location 的租赁义里。

items.en: English adopts locate in the 17c. with the sense 'to place or establish in a position'. It is a learned Latin borrowing, not an inherited word.
items.cn: 英语在 17 世纪引入 locate，义为“放置或安置于某位置”。它是学术性的拉丁借词，不是继承词。

items.en: The sense 'to find the exact position of' is recorded in the late 19c., first associated with surveying and marking land in North America.
items.cn: “找出确切位置”这一义项记录于 19 世纪晚期，最初与北美土地测量和标界有关。

items.en: Modern English extends locate to faults, files, signals, and genes. Be located becomes the standard way to state where a building or institution stands.
items.cn: 现代英语把 locate 扩展到故障、文件、信号和基因。be located 成为说明建筑或机构坐落何处的标准说法。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin place root or the loc- shape; the second separates finding, situating, positioning, and detecting.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语“地点”词根或 loc- 词形；第二组区分“找到”“坐落”“安置”和“探测”。

entries.definition: a place or position, or the act of placing something. It is the noun built directly on locate.
entries.definitionCN: 地点、位置，或放置的行为。它是直接由 locate 构成的名词。

entries.definition: a particular area or neighbourhood. It comes from local plus -ity, both from locus.
entries.definitionCN: 特定地区或街区。它由 local 加 -ity 构成，二者都出自 locus。

entries.definition: a railway engine. It joins locus 'place' with movere 'to move', so it moves from place to place, not from locate.
entries.definitionCN: 铁路机车。它把 locus“地点”与 movere“移动”结合，表示“从一地移到另一地”，并非来自 locate。

entries.definition: to discover something, often by chance or after searching. It is broader than locate and does not require an exact position.
entries.definitionCN: 发现某物，常是偶然或经搜寻而得到。它比 locate 宽泛，不要求确切位置。

entries.definition: to place something in a particular context or position. It is formal and common in the passive, like be situated.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物置于特定语境或位置。它较正式，常像 be situated 一样用于被动。

entries.definition: to put something in a chosen place. It stresses the choice of placement rather than the search for coordinates.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物放在选定的位置。它强调有意的摆放，而不是寻找坐标。

entries.definition: to discover that something is present, often with an instrument. It reports presence, while locate reports position.
entries.definitionCN: 发现某物存在，常用仪器。它报告“存在”，而 locate 报告“位置”。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin place word locus, the everyday phrase be located in, and the modern locator and GPS.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语地点词 locus、日常短语 be located in，以及现代的 locator 与 GPS。

normal.en: Locus means 'place'; locate is the verb that gives something a place or finds the place it has.
normal.cn: locus 意为“地点”；locate 就是给某物一个地点，或找到它已有的地点。

normal.en: Be located in is the standard phrase for where a building, office, or city stands.
normal.cn: be located in 是说明建筑、办事处或城市坐落何处的标准短语。

normal.en: To locate a fault is to put a finger on the exact point where a system fails.
normal.cn: locate a fault 就是把手指按到系统失效的那个确切点上。

normal.en: A locator is the device that does the locating: a GPS unit, a radio tag, or a sonar beacon.
normal.cn: locator 是执行定位的装置：全球定位仪、无线电标签或声呐信标。

normal.en: Location and locality both come from locus, one naming a point and the other a neighbourhood.
normal.cn: location 与 locality 都出自 locus，一个命名一个点，另一个命名一片街区。

abstract.en: A pin dropped on a paper map: the whole world is flattened, and one point is chosen.
abstract.cn: 一枚图钉落在纸质地图上：整个世界被压平，其中一个点被选中。

abstract.en: A coordinate grid: the place is not a thing but a pair of numbers where two lines cross.
abstract.cn: 一张坐标网格：地点不是一个物件，而是两条线相交处的一对数字。

abstract.en: A searchlight sweeps a dark field, then locks onto one spot; locating is the moment the beam stops moving.
abstract.cn: 探照灯扫过黑暗的场地，然后锁定一处；定位就是光束停止移动的那一刻。

examples.en: The app can locate your phone within a few metres.
examples.cn: 这个应用能在几米范围内定位你的手机。

examples.en: The new campus is located beside the river.
examples.cn: 新校区坐落在河边。

examples.en: Investigators located the leak beneath the kitchen floor.
examples.cn: 调查人员确定了厨房地板下的漏水点。

dict_mnemonic.text: “楼凯特”——凯特在楼里找到了自己的座位 → locate 找到位置

root: 拉丁语 locare“放置”，来自 locus“地点”；核心是“给某物指定或找到它的位置”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of locate, all from the Latin idea of a place: find the place, occupy a place, give a place, settle an institution, pinpoint a fault, fix a signal, find a passage, map a gene, and finally the boundary between finding and pinpointing.
sensesIntro.cn: locate 的九个义项都出自拉丁语“地点”这一观念：找到地点、占据地点、给予地点、让机构落户、锁定故障、确定信号、查到段落、标出基因，最后是“发现”与“精确定位”的边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pin is placed on one exact point of a map.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚图钉被按在地图的某一个精确点上。

branches.en: FINDING: searching ends when the exact point is identified, whether it is a person or a fault.
branches.cn: 寻找：当确切点被认出时搜索结束，无论对象是人还是故障。

branches.en: POSITION: a thing either occupies a place or is deliberately given one.
branches.cn: 位置：某物要么占据一个地点，要么被有意赋予一个地点。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONS AND TEXTS: a branch settles on a site, and a reader puts a finger on a passage.
branches.cn: 机构与文本：分支在场地落户，读者把手指按到某个段落。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT: instruments and genetic maps turn place into coordinates.
branches.cn: 测量：仪器与遗传图谱把地点变成坐标。

branches.en: BOUNDARY: locate demands an exact position, unlike the broader find.
branches.cn: 边界：locate 要求确切位置，不同于更宽泛的 find。

intro.en: Locate is a Latin verb borrowed whole. English adds -ion, -or, -ed and the prefix re- to build location, locator, located and relocate.
intro.cn: locate 是整体借入的拉丁动词。英语通过 -ion、-or、-ed 以及前缀 re- 构成 location、locator、located 与 relocate。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on locus 'place': local, locality, allocate and locomotion all assign, belong to, or move through a place.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族建立在 locus“地点”上：local、locality、allocate、locomotion 都涉及指派地点、属于某地或穿行于地点之间。

items.meaning: a place or position; the act of locating
items.meaningCN: 位置；地点；定位行为（-ion 构成行为或结果名词）
items.example: The location of the new station has not been decided.
items.exampleCN: 新车站的位置尚未确定。

items.meaning: a device or person that finds positions
items.meaningCN: 定位器；定位装置（-or 表示执行该动作的物）
items.example: The rescue team carried a radio locator.
items.exampleCN: 救援队携带了一台无线电定位器。

items.meaningCN: 位于……的；坐落于……的（-ed 构成形容词）
items.example: The office is located above the library.
items.exampleCN: 办公室位于图书馆上方。

items.meaning: to move something to a new place
items.meaningCN: 迁移；重新安置（re- 表示“再次、重新”）
items.example: The factory relocated to a larger site.
items.exampleCN: 工厂迁到了更大的场地。

items.example: Every member of the family rests on this noun.
items.exampleCN: 这一词族的每个成员都建立在这个名词上。

items.example: The stem carries the idea of place into English.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干把“地点”带入英语。

items.example: It forms the verb locate from the place noun.
items.exampleCN: 它由“地点”名词构成动词 locate。

items.example: It forms location, the act or result of placing.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 location，即定位的动作或结果。

items.meaning: to place together; to occur together
items.example: The two terms collocate in academic writing.
items.exampleCN: 这两个词在学术写作中常搭配出现。

latinEntries.meaning: a particular place or position; in genetics, the site of a gene
latinEntries.meaningCN: 地点；位置；基因座（直接来自拉丁语 locus）
地方的；当地的（与特定地区有关）

latinEntries.meaning: to assign something for a particular purpose
latinEntries.meaningCN: 分配；拨给（把资源“放置”到某个用途上）

latinEntries.meaning: movement from one place to another
latinEntries.meaningCN: 移动；运动（从一个地点移动到另一个地点）

definition_zh: 地点；位置；定位；外景拍摄地；存储位置
definition_en: a particular place or position, the act of finding it, or a real place used for filming
core_image: 地图上一枚被按下的图钉，把所有描述收束到一个点上
scene: 制片人摊开地图，用铅笔圈住河湾边的一排旧仓房。The warehouses by the river became the location for the opening scene.
sceneCN: 这里是「外景拍摄地」（第 3 个义项：剧组在摄影棚外实拍的地方）；句意为河边那排旧仓房成了开场戏的外景地。可辨物件：地图、铅笔圈、仓房。

pos.zh: 地点；位置；定位；外景拍摄地；存储位置

derivatives.zh: 与 location 同出拉丁语 locare，义为「找出位置；安置」
由 location 加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「位置的；地点方面的」
由 relocate 加 -ion 构成，义为「迁移；重新安置」

senses.title: A particular place or position
senses.definition: the place where someone or something is, or where an event happens
senses.definitionCN: 某人或某物所在、或某事发生的地方
senses.example: The hotel is in a quiet location near the park.
senses.exampleCN: 这家旅馆位于公园附近一处安静的地段。
senses.why: Latin locatio named the act of placing something, and English turned that act into the place that results from it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 locatio 指「放置」这个动作，英语由此转而指放置之后形成的那个地点。

senses.title: The act of finding where something is
senses.definition: the process of discovering or fixing the exact place of something
senses.definitionCN: 发现或确定某物确切位置的过程
senses.example: The location of the missing boat took the coast guard three days.
senses.exampleCN: 找到那条失踪小船的位置花了海岸警卫队三天。
senses.why: The noun can still name the action behind the place, so it covers the search as well as the spot finally found.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词仍能指地点背后的动作，所以既能指找到的那个点，也能指寻找这件事。

senses.title: A place used for filming outside a studio
senses.definition: a real place used for shooting a film or television scene instead of a built set
senses.definitionCN: 用来拍摄电影或电视场景的真实地点，而不是搭建的布景
senses.example: The crew spent two weeks at a mountain location.
senses.exampleCN: 摄制组在一个山区外景地待了两周。
senses.why: Film work needed a word for the real place standing in for a fictional one, and location was ready to carry that meaning.
senses.whyCN: 影视工作需要一个词来指代替代虚构场景的真实地点，location 正好承接了这个意思。

senses.title: A position in memory or on a disk
senses.definition: a place in a computer's memory or storage where a piece of data is kept
senses.definitionCN: 计算机内存或存储中保存某条数据的位置
senses.example: The program writes each record to a fixed location in memory.
senses.exampleCN: 程序把每条记录写到内存中一个固定的位置。
senses.why: Once a place can be pointed to precisely, machines borrow the word for the address where data sits.
senses.whyCN: 一旦一个地点能被精确指出，机器也用这个词来指数据所在的地址。

intro.en: Location is the Latin noun for a placing, built on the verb to place, and it reached English through French.
intro.cn: location 是拉丁语中表示「放置」的名词，建立在动词「放置」之上，经法语进入英语。

items.en: The Latin noun locus meant a place or spot and supplied the stem for the whole family.
items.cn: 拉丁语名词 locus 意为地方、地点，为整族词提供了词干。

items.en: The verb locare meant to place or set something somewhere, and it gave the action behind the noun.
items.cn: 动词 locare 意为把某物放置在某处，提供了名词背后的动作。

items.en: Locatio named a placing, and in legal Latin it could also mean a letting or a lease of property.
items.cn: locatio 指放置，在拉丁法律用语里也可指财产的出租。

items.en: Old French location carried the sense of a lease or a placing, and English borrowed the form.
items.cn: 古法语 location 带有出租或安置的意思，英语借用了这个词形。

items.en: Modern English made location the ordinary word for a place, then extended it to film sets and memory addresses.
items.cn: 现代英语让 location 成为指地点的常用词，随后扩展到影视外景与内存地址。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the Latin stem of placing; the near-meaning group collects nouns for a place in space.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「放置」词干上的词；近义组收表示空间位置的各类名词。

entries.definition: To find the exact place of something.
entries.definitionCN: 找出某物的确切位置。

entries.definition: Belonging to one particular place.
entries.definitionCN: 属于某一特定地方的。

entries.definition: A neighbourhood or a small area.
entries.definitionCN: 街区；小区。

entries.definition: The act of moving to a different place.
entries.definitionCN: 迁往另一地点的行为；迁移。

entries.definition: A piece of ground set aside for a building or an event.
entries.definitionCN: 供建筑或活动使用的一块场地。

entries.definition: The place where something stands in relation to others.
entries.definitionCN: 某物相对于其他事物所处的位置。

entries.definition: A small area or a particular point.
entries.definitionCN: 一小块地方；某个特定地点。

entries.definition: The place where an event is held.
entries.definitionCN: 举办活动的场所。

normalIntro.en: Location is the noun of placing: it can name the act, the resulting spot, and the special places films and computers point to.
normalIntro.cn: location 是「放置」的名词形式：它能指动作，能指由此形成的地点，也能指影视与计算机特指的位置。

normal.en: Location comes from Latin locatio, a placing, built on the verb locare.
normal.cn: location 来自拉丁语 locatio，意为放置，建立在动词 locare 之上。

normal.en: The suffix -tion turns the act of placing into the thing or result, here the place itself.
normal.cn: 后缀 -tion 把「放置」这个动作变成事物或结果，在这里就是那个地点。

normal.en: On location is a film phrase: the crew shoots where the story is supposed to happen.
normal.cn: on location 是影视用语：剧组在故事该发生的地方实拍。

normal.en: Locate is the verb, location the noun, and both keep the same Latin stem.
normal.cn: locate 是动词，location 是名词，两者共用同一拉丁词干。

normal.en: A prime location is one that everyone wants, which shows the word carries value as well as position.
normal.cn: prime location 指人人都想要的地段，说明这个词除位置之外还带着价值判断。

abstract.en: A place becomes a word only when someone needs to point at it.
abstract.cn: 一个地方只有在有人需要指认它时才变成一个词。

abstract.en: Location turns empty space into a spot with a name and a purpose.
abstract.cn: location 把空白的空间变成一个有名字、有用途的点。

abstract.en: The word travels from leases to film sets to memory chips without losing its centre.
abstract.cn: 这个词从租约走到片场，再到内存芯片，始终没有丢掉中心。

examples.en: The meeting will be held at a location outside the city centre.
examples.cn: 会议将在市中心以外的一处地点举行。

examples.en: The film was shot on location in the northern mountains.
examples.cn: 这部影片在北方山区实地拍摄。

examples.en: Please confirm the location of the server room.
examples.cn: 请确认机房的位置。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「啰个神」——地图上圈来圈去，就为找准那一个地点；记住 location 是「地点」。

root: 拉丁语 locus（地方）→ 动词 locare（放置）→ 名词 locatio（放置、出租）→ 古法语 location → 英语 location；同族词多与「地点、定位」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a spot in space; the senses then split into the act of finding it, the real place a film uses, and the address data occupies.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是空间中的某个点；义项由此分出寻找它的动作、影片采用的真实地点，以及数据所占的地址。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pin pressed into a map, gathering everything said about a place into one point.
core.cn: 核心意象：地图上一枚被按下的图钉，把关于一个地方的所有说法收束到一个点上。

branches.en: a hotel standing quietly beside a park
branches.cn: 旅馆安静地立在公园旁边

branches.en: a coast guard chart marked with a last known point
branches.cn: 海岸警卫队海图上标出的最后已知位置

branches.en: cameras and lights set up among real warehouses
branches.cn: 摄像机和灯架在真实仓房之间架起

branches.en: a record written to a numbered cell in a chip
branches.cn: 一条记录写进芯片里一个编号的格子

branches.en: a map full of pins marking chosen places
branches.cn: 一张插满图钉、标出选定地点的地图

intro.en: The word is the Latin noun of placing plus the English noun suffix -tion, so its parts all describe putting something somewhere.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「放置」的名词加上英语名词后缀 -tion，所以它的各部分都在说「把东西放到某处」。

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun locus, the verb locare and the noun locatio form one chain of placing, and English took the last link as location.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语名词 locus、动词 locare 与名词 locatio 构成一条「放置」的链，英语取最后一环为 location。

definition_zh: 锁；锁具；锁上；卡住；一绺头发；船闸
definition_en: to fasten something with a key or a catch, or the fastening device itself, a strand of hair, or a canal gate
core_image: 钥匙一转，锁舌滑进扣槽，门与门框从此扣成一体
scene: 夜里的院门半掩着，她伸手把铁锁扣好才上楼。She locked the gate and checked it twice before leaving.
sceneCN: 这里是「锁上、用锁锁住」（第 1 个义项：用钥匙或扣件把门关牢）；句意为她把院门锁好，走前还检查了两遍。可辨物件：院门、铁锁、楼道灯。

derivatives.zh: 由 lock 加表示相反动作的前缀 un- 构成，义为「开锁」
由 pad 与 lock 复合而成，义为「挂锁」
由 lock 与表示工匠的 smith 复合而成，义为「锁匠」
由 lock 加表示容器的后缀 -er 构成，义为「带锁的储物柜」

senses.title: To fasten something with a lock
senses.definition: to close and secure a door, box or vehicle with a key or a catch so that it cannot be opened easily
senses.definitionCN: 用钥匙或扣件把门、箱子或车辆关紧，使别人不容易打开
senses.example: She locked the door and put the key in her pocket.
senses.exampleCN: 她锁上门，把钥匙放进口袋。
senses.why: The Old English noun loc named the fastening itself, and the verb grew out of the act of turning that fastening shut.
senses.whyCN: 古英语名词 loc 本指扣件本身，动词义就是从「把这扣件扣上」这个动作长出来的。

senses.title: To become stuck and unable to move
senses.definition: to become fixed in one position, so that a part cannot turn or move freely
senses.definitionCN: 固定在某个位置，使某个部件无法转动或自由活动
senses.example: The wheels locked when he hit the brake hard.
senses.exampleCN: 他猛踩刹车时车轮抱死了。
senses.why: Once a lock is shut, nothing moves through it; applied to machines, the same image means a part that will not turn.
senses.whyCN: 锁一旦扣上，什么东西都过不去；用在机械上，同一个意象就指再也转不动的部件。

senses.title: The fastening device itself
senses.definition: a device with a key, a dial or a code that keeps a door or container shut
senses.definitionCN: 用钥匙、转盘或密码让门或容器保持关闭的装置
senses.example: The old trunk had a heavy brass lock.
senses.exampleCN: 这只旧箱子配着一把沉重的黄铜锁。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, the thing you hold in your hand, and every other sense spreads out from it.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，即你手里握着的那个物件，其余义项都从它扩散出去。

senses.title: A strand or small bunch of hair
senses.definition: a small quantity of hair that hangs or grows together as one piece
senses.definitionCN: 共同垂下或长在一起的一小束头发
senses.example: A lock of hair fell across her forehead.
senses.exampleCN: 一绺头发垂落在她额前。
senses.why: Hair that holds together in one clump looks like something fastened, so the word for a fastening was reused for a bunch of hair.
senses.whyCN: 头发聚成一束，看起来就像被扣住的东西，于是表示扣件的词又被用来指一束头发。

senses.title: A section of a canal with gates
senses.definition: a part of a canal closed off by gates, where the water level is raised or lowered for boats
senses.definitionCN: 运河上用闸门隔出的一段，通过升降水位让船只通过
senses.example: The barge waited for the lock to fill with water.
senses.exampleCN: 驳船等着船闸注满水。
senses.why: A canal lock works by shutting water in or out, which is exactly what a lock does to a door.
senses.whyCN: 船闸靠把水关进或放出而工作，这正是锁对门所做的那件事。

intro.en: Lock is a native English word whose deeper Germanic origin is reconstructed rather than recorded, and it has no reliable Latin relative.
intro.cn: lock 是英语本土词，更早的日耳曼语来源属于重构而非有记录的原形，也没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

items.en: The fastening is generally traced to a Germanic root luk-, whose exact shape is reconstructed rather than recorded.
items.cn: 这类扣件一般认为可追到日耳曼语词根 luk-，其确切形式属于重构，而不是有记录的原形。

items.en: Old English loc meant a fastening, a bolt or a barrier, and it also named a lock of hair.
items.cn: 古英语 loc 指扣件、门闩或障碍，同时也指一绺头发。

items.en: Middle English lock kept both the device and the hair sense, and the verb locken appeared for shutting something with it.
items.cn: 中古英语 lock 同时保留器具与头发两个义项，动词 locken 出现，表示用锁具关住。

items.en: Modern English added canal locks, and the verb widened to mean any part that jams and will not move.
items.cn: 现代英语增添了船闸义，动词也扩展到指任何卡住不动的部件。

items.en: Today the word covers keys and doors, traffic queues, canal gates, and a single strand of hair.
items.cn: 今天这个词覆盖钥匙与门、排队的车辆、船闸闸门以及一束头发。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on lock or closely spelled compounds; the near-meaning group collects fastening devices and the act of fastening.
note.cn: 形近组收由 lock 构成或拼写相近的复合词；近义组收各类扣件以及「扣紧」这个动作。

entries.definition: A small bar that keeps a door or gate closed.
entries.definitionCN: 让门或栅栏保持关闭的小闩。

entries.definition: A sliding bar used to fasten a door.
entries.definitionCN: 用来闩门的滑动横杆。

entries.definition: To attach or close something firmly.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物牢牢固定或关紧。

entries.definition: A small device that holds two parts together.
entries.definitionCN: 把两部分扣在一起的小扣件。

normalIntro.en: Lock is an Old English word for a fastening, and its many senses all come from one picture: something held shut.
normalIntro.cn: lock 是古英语中表示扣件的词，它的众多义项都出自同一个画面：某样东西被扣住不放。

normal.en: Lock is an Old English word for a fastening, older than any Latin borrowing in this entry.
normal.cn: lock 是古英语中表示扣件的词，比这条词条里的任何拉丁借词都古老。

normal.en: Unlock is simply un- plus lock, the prefix undoing the fastening.
normal.cn: unlock 就是 un- 加 lock，前缀把扣紧的状态解掉。

normal.en: A lock of hair is not a different word: hair that holds together looks fastened.
normal.cn: a lock of hair 并不是另一个词：头发聚成一束，看起来像被扣住了。

normal.en: Lock up, lock in and lock out all keep the same core of shutting something in or out.
normal.cn: lock up、lock in 与 lock out 都保留着「把东西关进或关外」这同一个核心。

normal.en: A canal lock locks water in or out, which is why the same word serves boats and doors.
normal.cn: 船闸把水关进或放出，所以同一个词能同时用于船和门。

abstract.en: A lock is a promise made in metal: only the right person passes.
abstract.cn: 锁是用金属做出的承诺：只有对的人才能通过。

abstract.en: When a wheel locks, the machine briefly behaves like a shut door.
abstract.cn: 车轮抱死时，机器短暂地像一扇关上的门。

abstract.en: The word joins a keyhole, a hair strand and a canal gate because all three are things that hold together or shut.
abstract.cn: 这个词把钥匙孔、一束头发和闸门连在一起，因为三者都是「扣住」或「关住」的东西。

examples.en: Remember to lock the back door before you leave.
examples.cn: 走之前记得把后门锁上。

examples.en: A thick lock of hair fell over her eyes.
examples.cn: 厚厚一绺头发垂到她眼睛上。

examples.en: The ship waited for the lock gates to open.
examples.cn: 船等着闸门打开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「落扣」——门一关，锁舌落进扣槽，咔一声就锁住了；记住 lock 是锁。

root: 古英语 loc（扣件、门闩，也指一束头发），一般认为与日耳曼语中表示「关闭、扣住」的词根有关，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is something held shut; the senses then spread from the device to its action, to a jammed part, to a clump of hair and to a canal gate.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「被扣住不放」；义项由器具扩散到动作、卡死的部件、一束头发，以及运河闸门。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a key turns, the bolt slides into its slot, and door and frame become one closed piece.
core.cn: 核心意象：钥匙一转，锁舌滑进扣槽，门与门框扣成一体。

branches.en: a key turning twice in a gate at night
branches.cn: 夜里钥匙在院门上转了两圈

branches.en: brake pads gripping a wheel that will not turn
branches.cn: 刹车片咬住再也转不动的车轮

branches.en: a barge rising slowly inside a canal lock
branches.cn: 驳船在船闸里缓缓上升

intro.cn: lock 是英语本土词，所以它的各部分由古英语形式加上现代前缀与复合成分组成，而不是拉丁语构件。

definition_zh: 原木；圆木；航海日志；记录簿；记录；累计达到（里程、工时）
definition_en: a thick piece of cut or fallen tree; an official written record of events on a ship or aircraft; to write down events or figures in such a record; to travel or work a stated amount that is added to a total
core_image: 斧头落下去，树干断成一截一截，木纹里还渗着树脂
scene: 码头边的空地上，卡车后挡板放下，几截树干滚了下来。A thick log rolled off the truck and landed in the mud.
sceneCN: 这里是「伐下的整段树干」（第 1 个义项：未经加工的原木）；句意为一段粗大的原木从卡车上滚下来，落进了泥地里。

pos.zh: 记录；把……记入日志；累计达到

derivatives.zh: 由 log 加表示「人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「伐木工；记录员」
由 log 加 -ing 构成，义为「伐木作业」
由 log 与 book 复合而成，义为「日志簿；记录本」
由 back 与 log 复合而成，义为「积压未办的工作」
由 log 与 in 复合而成，义为「登录」

senses.title: A thick piece of cut tree
senses.definition: a thick piece of wood cut from a tree, or a whole trunk lying where it fell
senses.definitionCN: 从树上砍下的粗大木段，或倒在地上未经处理的整根树干
senses.example: The cabin walls were built from rough logs.
senses.exampleCN: 小木屋的墙是用粗糙的原木垒起来的。
senses.why: Middle English logge already meant a lump of wood, and this concrete sense has stayed at the centre of the word ever since.
senses.whyCN: 中古英语 logge 已经指一截木头，这个最具体的义项从中古一直留到今天，是整组词义的中心。

senses.title: An official record of a voyage or flight
senses.definition: an official written record of events kept on a ship, an aircraft or a machine
senses.definitionCN: 船、飞机或机器上保存的正式事件记录
senses.example: The captain wrote the storm into the ship's log.
senses.exampleCN: 船长把这场风暴写进了航海日志。
senses.why: Sailors measured speed by throwing a weighted piece of wood overboard and reading the line; the figures went into a book, and the book took the name of the wood.
senses.whyCN: 船员把一块系着重物的木头抛进海里测速，再读线上的刻度；数字记进本子，本子便沿用了那块木头的名字。

senses.title: To write something down in a record
senses.definition: to write an event, figure or message into an official record as it happens
senses.definitionCN: 把发生的事情、数字或消息在发生时写入正式记录
senses.example: Officers logged every radio message during the night.
senses.exampleCN: 夜里，值班人员把每一条无线电消息都记了下来。
senses.why: Once log named the book, the same word could name the act of writing in it, so the record and the recording share one form.
senses.whyCN: 当 log 指那本簿子之后，同一个词自然也能指在簿子上书写这件事，于是「记录」和「被记录的内容」共用一个形式。

senses.title: To add up distance or working time
senses.definition: to travel or work an amount that is added to a running total
senses.definitionCN: 走过的距离或工作的时间被累加进一个总数
senses.example: The old bus has logged more than a million kilometres.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆旧巴士累计跑了一百多万公里。
senses.why: A logbook keeps a running total, so the verb came to mean reaching a figure that the book will hold.
senses.whyCN: 日志簿记的是一路累加的总数，所以动词又指达到某个会被写进簿子的数字。

intro.en: Log appears in Middle English as a word for a block of wood, and its further origin is uncertain; the record sense grew out of sailors measuring speed with a wooden chip.
intro.cn: log 在中古英语里就指一截木头，更早的来源不确定；记录义则从船员用木块测速这件事上长出来。

items.en: The word is first recorded in Middle English as logge, a block of wood, and no earlier form is securely attested.
items.cn: 这个词最早见于中古英语，写作 logge，指一截木头；更早的形式没有可靠的书面证据。

items.en: Logge named a cut block or a fallen trunk, the rough timber used for walls and for firewood.
items.cn: logge 指砍下的木块或倒下的树干，就是用来垒墙和烧火的粗木料。

items.en: Some dictionaries suggest a connection with Scandinavian words for something lying down, but the link is not certain.
items.cn: 一些词典认为它与斯堪的纳维亚语中表示「躺倒之物」的词有关，但这一联系并不确定。

items.en: A weighted wooden chip was thrown overboard to measure a ship's speed, and the readings were kept in a log book.
items.cn: 人们把一块加重的小木板抛到船外测速，读数记在航海日志里。

items.en: The word extends to any systematic record, then to computer sign-ins and to totals of distance or hours.
items.cn: 词义扩展到任何系统化的记录，再进入计算机登录，也表示里程或工时的累计。

note.en: The look-alike group is built from log plus common English elements; the near-meaning group gathers words for wood and for written records.
note.cn: 形近组由 log 与常见英语成分组合而成；近义组收表示木材和书面记录的词。

entries.definitionCN: 记录事件的正式簿子；日志簿。

entries.definition: A person who cuts timber or keeps a record.
entries.definitionCN: 伐木的人，或负责记录的人。

entries.definition: The business of cutting trees for timber.
entries.definitionCN: 砍树取木材的行业；伐木。

entries.definition: Work that has piled up and is still waiting.
entries.definitionCN: 堆积起来尚未处理的工作；积压。

entries.definition: The act of signing into a computer system.
entries.definitionCN: 登录计算机系统的动作；登录。

entries.definition: Wood prepared for building, or standing trees.
entries.definitionCN: 备好的建筑木材，或尚未砍伐的树木。

entries.definition: A book in which a person writes about each day.
entries.definitionCN: 逐日写下经历的簿子；日记。

entries.definition: A serious record of events or a periodical about them.
entries.definitionCN: 对事件的正式记录，或刊载这类内容的期刊。

entries.definition: A written account of facts kept for the future.
entries.definitionCN: 为日后查阅而留下的事实记载。

normalIntro.en: Log starts as a plain word for a block of wood; the written record comes from the wooden chip sailors threw into the sea.
normalIntro.cn: log 起初只是「一截木头」的朴素说法；书面记录义则来自船员抛进海里的那块木片。

normal.en: Middle English wrote logge for a cut block of wood, and that solid sense never left the word.
normal.cn: 中古英语把砍下的一截木头写作 logge，这个实在的意思一直没有离开这个词。

normal.en: Sailors threw a weighted chip into the water, read the line, and wrote the figures in a book, so the book was named after the wood.
normal.cn: 船员把加重的小木片抛进水里，读线上的刻度，再把数字写进本子，本子便跟着木头得了名。

normal.en: Logger adds -er to log: the person who cuts the timber or keeps the record.
normal.cn: logger 在 log 后加 -er：砍木头的人，或负责记记录的人。

normal.en: Logbook is log and book joined directly, a book that holds the entries.
normal.cn: logbook 是 log 与 book 直接拼在一起，指收纳这些记录的本子。

normal.en: Backlog is back plus log: entries that piled up behind the rest, now any unfinished work.
normal.cn: backlog 是 back 加 log：堆在后面的记录，如今指任何积压未办的工作。

abstract.en: A cut block and a record book share one word, which suggests English treats a countable thing and a checkable trace as close neighbours.
abstract.cn: 一截木头和一本记录簿共用一个词，说明英语把「可数的东西」和「可查的痕迹」看得很近。

abstract.en: The chip thrown overboard is a reminder that a record is built from readings someone can check, not from memory.
abstract.cn: 抛到船外的那块木片提醒人：记录靠的是一次次可以核对的读数，而不是记忆。

abstract.en: Turn the pages of a log and time is cut into lines, which is the most practical picture this word offers.
abstract.cn: 一页页翻日志，时间就被切成一行一行，这是这个词最实用的画面。

examples.en: A fallen log blocked the path through the forest.
examples.cn: 一段倒下的原木挡住了穿过森林的小路。

examples.en: The pilot logged six hours of flying time that week.
examples.cn: 那名飞行员那一周累计飞行了六个小时。

examples.en: Every visitor is logged at the front desk.
examples.cn: 每位来访者都在前台做了登记。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「烙个」——把每天的事烙在本子上，就成了日志；log 既是木头，也是记录。

root: 来源不确定：中古英语 logge 已指「砍下的木块」，一般认为可能与斯堪的纳维亚语中表示「躺倒的树」的词有关，但没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The concrete sense is a cut trunk; the record sense grew from sailors writing down what a floating chip told them, and from there the word covers any systematic account.
sensesIntro.cn: 具体的义项是砍下的树干；记录义从船员把浮木读出的数字写下来开始，再扩展到任何系统化的记载。
